study_design_notes.blinding: not consistently blinded across included trials

evidence.summary: McCulloch et al. 2006 (JCO 24(3):419-430) pooled 34 RCTs (2815 patients) and found reduced risk of death at 12 months (RR 0.67) and improved tumor response (RR 1.34) when Astragalus-based formulas were added to platinum chemotherapy. The meta-analysis's own authors state that because several included studies were of poor quality, these findings need confirmation in well-designed trials -- reappraisal against current systematic-review and risk-of-bias standards is required before any certainty upgrade.

cards.limitations: Included-trial quality is explicitly flagged as poor by the meta-analysis's own authors; randomization, blinding, and reporting quality require independent re-appraisal against current standards; exact formula composition varies across the 34 pooled trials and is not uniform.
cards.what_was_not_shown: No single, currently reproducible, high-quality trial demonstrating a specific Astragalus-containing formula improves survival in advanced NSCLC with platinum chemotherapy; the pooled positive signal is not the same as a practice-ready recommendation.

publication_integrity.notes: No integrity concern identified on the meta-analysis itself; included-trial quality is the flagged issue, not misconduct.

evidence.summary: PMC11734505 (received 2024-10-26, published 2025-01) reviews TCM-derived formulations in cancer immunotherapy. Verified via direct fetch: cited findings are predominantly cell/animal/mechanistic, with limited human clinical trial data acknowledged by the review itself. The review also contains this exact unsafe, unsupported statement, which this proposal explicitly does NOT reproduce or endorse: 'Western medicine usually eliminates tumors through sectioning and surgery, which inevitably leads to the consequences of tumor spread.' Surgical resection is standard, evidence-based curative-intent treatment for many solid tumors; no card in this proposal may imply that surgery causes cancer spread.

cards.limitations: Predominantly preclinical (cell-line and animal-model) evidence; the review's own causal/efficacy language exceeds what the underlying preclinical data support; no qualifying human trial was independently verified for any single formula discussed.
cards.what_was_not_shown: No human efficacy or safety data suitable for any patient-facing statement; no support whatsoever for any claim that surgery promotes cancer spread.

publication_integrity.notes: The article itself is not retracted or flagged by its publisher in this pass, but this proposal records and refuses to reproduce its unsafe surgery-related statement, and treats its causal/efficacy language as exceeding its own evidence throughout.

evidence.summary: Raw Tripterygium wilfordii and its extracts can cause serious multiorgan toxicity: hepatic, renal, hematologic, gastrointestinal, and reproductive (including infertility and menstrual irregularity). Isolated compounds (triptolide, celastrol) show preclinical anticancer signals but are not established as safe or effective in humans.

cards.limitations: This card intentionally separates a toxicity/avoid record (raw herb) from a preclinical record (isolated compounds); neither implies the other's status.
cards.what_was_not_shown: No human efficacy or safety data supporting self-use of the raw herb for any indication in a cancer patient.

safety.standard_care_statement: This survey supports a general disclosure/medication-reconciliation practice (ask patients what they are using), not any specific product recommendation.
